_why: Row 'refuse auto-generated parametrize ids in a spec's `test`': --check-anchors reports a mutation row whose `test` names a pytest AUTO param id (`<argname><N>`, given to a non-literal value), because inserting a case before it silently re-points the row at another case that still passes. Static only, advisory detail line, never a summary word. Each mutant removes one guard of that report.

mutations.name: A1: IGNORE EXPLICIT IDS. A parametrize whose cases carry `pytest.param(..., id=...)` is flagged as auto, so every hand-named row reads as a hazard.
A2: TREAT EVERY VALUE AS NON-LITERAL. `allow-rc1` beside an int-valued `rc` is flagged again: the calibration false positive (H4) the literal check removed.
mutations.find: if not all(_is_literal(v) for v in values[hit]):

mutations.name: A3: AN UNREADABLE TEST FILE READS AS OK. The could-not-check case takes the same branch as the checked-and-clean one.
A4: AN ID FROM OUTSIDE ANY PARAMETRIZE READS AS OK. Fixture `params=` and `pytest_generate_tests` ids are silently passed instead of reported as cannot-judge.
mutations.find: if not matched and not calls:

mutations.name: A5: STOP SPLITTING STACKED IDS. `cfg0-fast` is inspected whole, never matches the identifier-plus-digits shape, and the auto `cfg0` goes unreported.
mutations.find: shaped = [s for s in param_id.split("-") if _AUTO_ID_SHAPE.fullmatch(s)]

mutations.name: A6: A NON-LITERAL CASE LIST READS AS OK. `parametrize("case", CASES)` cannot be judged statically, and skipping it hides exactly the cases built in a loop.
A7: COMPUTE THE FINDING, NEVER PRINT IT. The sweep keeps the result but no reader of --check-anchors ever sees it.
